title: Two Coworkers Talk About Turning Off Notifications
script: Dewi: [frustrated] Fajar, I cannot focus today. My phone keeps buzzing every few minutes, and I lose my train of thought.
Fajar: [calmly] What kind of notifications are you getting? Maybe some of them are not even necessary.
Dewi: [sighing] Everything. Messages, app updates, news alerts, even a game I barely play anymore.
Fajar: [gently] Can I suggest something? I turned off almost all my notifications a few months ago.
Dewi: [surprised] All of them? Aren't you worried about missing something important?
Fajar: [smiling] I kept messages and calls, since those are usually urgent. Everything else, I turned off completely.
Dewi: [thoughtful] What happened after you did that?
Fajar: [warmly] Honestly, it was quiet, in a good way. I stopped picking up my phone every few minutes.
Dewi: [curious] Did you check the apps less, or did you just check them at different times?
Fajar: [explaining] Different times. Now I open news and social apps twice a day, on purpose, instead of constantly.
Dewi: [considering] I never thought about choosing when to check things. I just react whenever my phone makes noise.
Fajar: [encouraging] Try it for one week. Turn off everything except messages and calls, and see how it feels.
Dewi: [thoughtful] I'm a little nervous, honestly. What if my team needs me urgently for something?
Fajar: [reassuring] You can always keep work messages on. The goal is removing the small, unimportant interruptions, not everything.
Dewi: [determined] Okay, I'll try it this afternoon. I'm curious how different my focus will feel tomorrow.
Fajar: [warmly] Let me know how it goes. It genuinely changed how calm my work days feel now.
Dewi: [thoughtful] I also want to try putting my phone in my bag during meetings, instead of on the table.
Fajar: [agreeing] That helps a lot too. Just seeing the screen light up can pull your attention away instantly.
Dewi: [smiling] Between the notifications and the meetings, I think I'll actually finish my reports on time this week.
Fajar: [warmly] That's the goal. Small changes like this add up more than people expect.
